subject: religious-studies
title: Applied Ethics: Business, Sex and Conscience
welcome_lead: Apply the four major ethical theories to business ethics, sexual ethics, and the disputed faculty of conscience.
meta_desc: A-Level Religious Studies adventure on applied ethics: business and sexual ethics, and theories of conscience from Aquinas to Freud.
final_note: You have applied Natural Law, Kantianism, Utilitarianism, and Situation Ethics to contemporary cases and to conscience itself.

concepts.def: The view (Freeman) that businesses have duties to all affected parties, not just shareholders.
Milton Friedman's view that the social responsibility of business is to increase its profits within the rules.
Disclosure by employees of wrongdoing; sometimes ethically required despite loyalty considerations.
Aquinas's innate disposition to grasp 'do good, avoid evil'.
Aquinas's application of synderesis to particular acts.
Freud's psychic agency that internalises parental and social prohibitions; his account of conscience.

walkthroughs.body_html: Milton Friedman's 1970 New York Times Magazine piece argued that managers' fiduciary duty is to shareholders. R. Edward Freeman's Strategic Management: A Stakeholder Approach (1984) countered with a broader account of duties. Kantians stress treating employees and customers as ends; Natural Law condemns intrinsic exploitation; utilitarians weigh long-term consequences; situationists ask what love requires.

Catholic teaching, drawing on Natural Law and Humanae Vitae (1968), holds that sexual acts must remain open to procreation and unitive love. Kant in Lectures on Ethics warns sexual desire risks reducing the other to a thing. Utilitarians focus on consent and consequences; Fletcher's situationism asks whether the most loving act in this case may bend traditional rules.

Aquinas distinguishes synderesis (the disposition) from conscientia (the act of judgement) in De Veritate. Newman's Letter to the Duke of Norfolk (1875) called conscience the 'aboriginal vicar of Christ'. Freud's The Ego and the Id (1923) reframed conscience as the superego, internalised parental prohibition - a reductive psychogenetic account contested by religious thinkers.

mcqs.q: What does utilitarianism say is right action?
options: Utilitarianism says you should always tell the truth.
The action that produces the greatest happiness for the greatest number — judged by consequences, not intentions or rules.
Virtue ethics is about following the Ten Commandments.
Whatever makes you personally happy is the right thing to do.

mcqs.q: What does Kant's categorical imperative require?
options: Treat others how you would like to be treated.
Acting only on maxims you could will to be universal laws, and treating people as ends in themselves, never merely as means.
Do whatever your conscience tells you to do.
Virtue ethics is about following the Ten Commandments.

mcqs.q: What is the focus of virtue ethics?
options: Virtue ethics tells you which specific actions are right and wrong.
Do whatever your conscience tells you to do.
On character and habits — becoming the kind of person who acts well, aiming at eudaimonia (flourishing) through practising virtues that lie between extremes.
Virtue ethics is about following the Ten Commandments.
